Not Recommended (and honestly, I should ve known better) 200 hours played. That s not a flex. That s a warning sign. You don t play this game anymore you maintain it like a second job you never applied for. You spawn naked on a beach with a rock and a torch. Sounds like a survival game, right? Wrong. It s a punishment loop disguised as progression. Within minutes you re reminded what the game actually is: Target practice for players with thousands of hours Free loot delivery service Background noise for someone screaming in voice chat There s no learning curve. Just a cliff. You think you re progressing, grinding resources, building something meaningful. In reality, you re just stockpiling items for the next guy who logs in while you re asleep. The building system is good technically. But what s the point of a good system when everything you build is temporary by design? You don t own anything in this game. You re just borrowing it until someone else takes it. The community gets described as chaotic or funny, but let s be honest: It s wildly inconsistent at best and straight-up unbearable at worst. For every genuinely funny interaction, you get ten that make you question why voice chat exists. And the time sink? Just one more run turns into hours of repetitive farming with zero payoff. Not because you made a mistake just because someone else had more time than you. At some point it stops being engaging and starts being exhausting. Pros: It hooks you (not in a good way) Solid mechanics wasted on a punishing loop Unpredictability mostly negative Cons: Progress means nothing longterm Encourages unhealthy play habits Community can be outright miserable Constant loss with no real payoff Playtime: Too much to justify Fun: Questionable Respect for my own time: Gone Would I recommend it? No Will I still play? Probably not and that s the problem

In my opinion, Valve has lost interest in CS2. While Deadlock receives major gameplay updates, reworks, new mechanics, and constant developer attention, CS2 feels abandoned. The cheating problem continues to frustrate players, trust in VAC is at an all-time low, and many long-time fans feel ignored. What makes it even worse is the growing feeling that Valve cares more about monetization than about the actual game. Some players believe that Valve would prefer more skin trading to happen directly through the Steam Market, where they collect fees, rather than through third-party marketplaces. Whether that's true or not, the lack of communication and focus on core issues has created a lot of distrust within the community. Counter-Strike used to be Valve's flagship competitive title. Today it feels like the game exists to generate revenue while anti-cheat, content updates, and player concerns take a back seat. Meanwhile, Deadlock gets the attention, innovation, and development effort that CS2 players have been asking for.

TLDR: CS2 is a no-no currently, lacks what CSGO had, community's infested with a major population of immature brats, problematics worming their way on both Casual and Comp modes, greed takes priority than the community, devs abandoned the game, and many other 99 problems we could list but am not going to tire myself with that. Starting with the first and foremost cardinal advice, I recommend against playing Counter-Strike 2 in its current state. It's the hollow promise that was never realized and also the reason that Counter-Strike Global Offensive deserved better than to be replaced by the game that's now left out to be severely rotten without any meaningful changes. The gameplay is as the same as you would've had it on Global Offensive, except this time it's practically turned into a barebones version that is not feeling the same. 2's Matchmaking modes are lacking where Global Offensive had much more on offer. You only have Casual, Deathmatch, Arms Race and Retakes. That, and the competitive modes such as Premier, Competitive and Wingman that I'm not ever keen on touching with a 10-foot pole because of the horrifyingly inconsistent anti-cheat that allows cheaters to illegitimately rank their way up through unprofessional means. On Casual matchmaking modes, you'd be lucky to have some coherent individuals that know how to play the game, but chances are there are plenty of rotten apples who will go out of their way to completely sabotage your normal session and just attempt to votekick you out of the lobby because they suck and thrive off their bloated egos, or if you're playing way better than everyone on your team. Just because you happen to play better doesn't mean the immature runts have enough reason to do a votekick over it, yet they do. Deathmatch? DON'T GET ME STARTED. Every map group has become infested with the botfarm problem that's been plaguing the mode for as long as it's still prevalent, yet nothing is done to outright use digital insecticide to brick the living daylights out of the lowly insect botfarm-operated accounts (with PRIME STATUS, mind you) that continue to worm their way into this mode for every weekly drop they can get. Arms Race is just plainly stripped down two Gun-Game maps and two Shoots maps. Not worth the effort IMO, since it's just mindless gun-rolling and I don't care much for it. Retakes is 4v3 straight-shot of the normal defusal mode but it's a genuinely 99 losing and 1 winning because you can't get teammates that constantly run into enemy players or sometimes get lucky if you have a team that aims to win. I even saw a duo of russian brats votekicking a singular teammate off the T side because they want to play duo and yet they lost because of it, that's how inept a harmfully immature majority of players are distinguished from the sane and mentally stable human players. Like Global Offensive, you can have plenty of skins for your weapons, gloves, even agents to make you look distinguished from the default agents on every map because for some ungodly reason factions had to be removed and put back in as standalone agents that you have to buy. You can already guess that some high-tier skins and items even cost a lotta real world money and it's not feasible to save money on when you got cases that you have to buy untradable keys for. The game may have stood solid in the beginning of its lifespan, but in the long-standing overtime it's worn out its welcome. No sane person should ever have to endure the majority of caustic dimwits within the playerbase who aim to sabotage your experience no matter the mode by being obnoxious and votekicking you for any reason to boost their bloated ego. And the fact that it's in a sordid state is inexcusable especially when greed takes priority within the high-ups and the devs have left the game and its players on life support. h1 Dead by Daylight Review h1 hr hr h2 Introduction h2 Dead by Daylight is Behaviour Interactive's asymmetric survival horror multiplayer and nearly a decade after launch, it is still the undisputed king of its genre. Four survivors scramble to repair generators and escape. One killer hunts them down using supernatural powers and brute force. Simple concept. Infinite depth. What started as a niche indie experiment in 2016 has grown into one of the biggest ongoing live-service games on PC and console and its best days are still being written right now. hr hr h2 Core Gameplay h2 No two matches ever feel the same, and that is genuinely impressive for a game with such a tight ruleset. The tension between repairing generators and staying hidden is perfectly calibrated every second matters The chases are pulse-pounding, with looping, vaulting, and mind-game mechanics that reward skill on both sides The skill check system keeps survivors constantly alert even during the quieter moments Playing killer feels completely different from survivor it is essentially two games sharing one map Totem cleansing, chest hunting, and hook rescues create natural moments of teamwork without voice chat The asymmetry is the magic. A coordinated survivor team that clicks perfectly is one of the most satisfying experiences in multiplayer gaming. An equally matched killer who reads their movements is just as thrilling from the other side. hr hr h2 Atmosphere Maps h2 Dead by Daylight's world The Entity's Realm is genuinely unsettling in a way most horror games fail to achieve. Each realm has its own distinct visual identity, from the industrial rot of MacMillan Estate to the clinical dread of L ry's Memorial Institute Fog, ambient sound, and darkness do more work than most AAA horror titles twice its budget Procedurally generated tile layouts ensure maps never feel identical between sessions The Entity's influence hooks, corrupted terrain, and those massive claw-like structures creates a constant sense of something ancient watching every trial Walking into a match on a dark foggy Coldwind Farm with distant heartbeats growing louder is still one of gaming's best slow-burn dread experiences. hr hr h2 The Roster Killers Survivors h2 This is where Dead by Daylight truly separates itself from every competitor it has inspired. b The killer roster is extraordinary. b Original creations like The Nurse, The Trapper, and The Artist sit alongside licensed legends Michael Myers, Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Chucky, Vecna, and many more. Each killer plays completely differently from the rest, with unique power kits that demand different strategies and counter-play from survivors. The licensed crossovers are handled with genuine care and respect for the source material. Seeing Michael Myers stalk you through corn fields exactly as he does in Halloween is a legitimately surreal experience. b Survivors matter just as much. b Original survivors have grown into beloved characters with deep lore across comics, tomes, and in-game stories. The survivor pool is now enormous, covering a wide range of personalities and backgrounds. hr hr h2 Perks, Builds Depth h2 Dead by Daylight's perk system is secretly one of the deepest build-crafting systems in any multiplayer game. Every killer and survivor comes with three unique perks that can be unlocked and mixed across the entire roster Build variety is enormous aggressive builds, stealth builds, generator rush strategies, and altruistic team-focused setups all work On the killer side, the difference between a proper perk-synergy build and a random selection is massive and immediately felt Add-ons and offerings add another layer of customization before a trial even begins The meta constantly evolves as Behaviour balances perks and introduces new ones with each chapter Learning the perk ecosystem is a genuinely rewarding long-term investment. The deeper you go, the more satisfying the game becomes. hr hr h2 Lore Tomes h2 Dead by Daylight's lore is criminally underrated and far richer than most players realize. The Tome system releases story chapters revealing the backstories of killers and survivors through beautifully written journal entries, cutscene memories, and in-world artifacts. The Entity itself is a fascinating cosmic horror concept a creature that feeds on hope and despair, pulling beings from across dimensions for millennia of suffering. If you have ever dismissed DbD as a game without story, the Tomes will genuinely surprise you. Characters like The Artist, The Dredge, and Jonah Vasquez carry some of the most compelling horror writing the genre has seen in years. hr hr h2 Problems h2 Dead by Daylight is exceptional, but it earns its complaints too. Balance remains an ongoing challenge certain killers and perk combinations feel overwhelmingly oppressive at lower skill levels Matchmaking can be inconsistent, occasionally placing new players against veterans with thousands of hours The community has a well-documented toxic streak post-game chat is often best left unread entirely Cosmetic pricing for licensed content is steep, and the archive grind feels padded in later tomes Some older maps have tile layouts that heavily favour one side, and reworks have been slow None of these are deal-breakers but they are real, and new players should know what they are walking into. Thick skin helps. hr hr h2 Final Thoughts h2 Dead by Daylight should not still be this good. Nearly a decade in, most live-service games have faded. DbD has grown into something genuinely special a game that keeps evolving its roster, its systems, and its world while never losing sight of the core loop that made it extraordinary in the first place. b If you love horror culture, it is the ultimate fan experience your favourite villains made playable, treated with real creative respect. b b If you love deep multiplayer games, the perk system alone will keep you theorycrafting for years. b Horrifying, tense, occasionally infuriating, deeply rewarding and completely impossible to put down once it gets its hooks in you. That last part is very much intentional. hr hr h2 Rating h2 9.2 10 One of the greatest live-service games ever made. Horror licensed content done right, endlessly deep build-crafting, and a tension loop that no competitor has managed to replicate after ten years of trying.

Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) stands as the successor to one of the most iconic tactical shooters in gaming history. By transitioning from the aging CS:GO engine to Source 2, Valve aimed to modernize the experience while preserving the core competitive integrity that defined the series for over two decades. --- The Good: Refined Mechanics and Competitive Depth Source 2 Engine: The visual overhaul is significant. Lighting, textures, and particle effects are drastically improved, making the game look sharper and more immersive. Dynamic Smoke Grenades: This is arguably the most impactful gameplay change. Smokes are now volumetric objects that interact with the environment. They react to bullets and explosions, allowing players to clear lines of sight temporarily a feature that adds an incredible layer of strategic depth. Sub-Tick Architecture: Valve introduced a new "sub-tick" update system intended to bridge the gap between high-tick rate servers and lower-tick environments. While controversial at launch, it fundamentally aims to make movement and shooting more responsive and consistent across all player tiers. The Premier Mode: The revamped matchmaking system offers a clear, ELO-based ranking path that feels more professional and rewarding than the traditional matchmaking ranks. The Fun: The "Culture" of CS Skin Economy: The digital economy surrounding CS2 is unmatched. Collecting, trading, and showcasing skins is a game in itself, often keeping players engaged even when they aren't actively grinding ranks. The Community Custom Servers: From intense "Surf" maps and "KZ" (parkour) servers to casual community modes, the social aspect of jumping into a server with friends remains the heart of the experience. The "Clutch" Moments: There is no adrenaline rush quite like being the last player alive in a 1v3 situation, successfully defusing the bomb, and hearing the roar of your teammates. These high-stakes moments are what make the game legendary. The Bad: Challenges and Frustrations Anti-Cheat Issues: Despite the introduction of "VAC Live," the game continues to struggle with cheaters in higher ranks. Many long-time players feel that the current anti-cheat system is insufficient to handle the evolving complexity of external software. Performance Inconsistency: While the Source 2 engine looks great, it demands more from hardware than its predecessor. Many players with mid-range setups have experienced inconsistent frame rates (stuttering) that can be fatal in a competitive shooter. Content Deficit: Since its release, many legacy maps, community game modes (like "Arms Race" or "Danger Zone" variations), and specific tactical elements from CS:GO have been slow to return or are missing entirely, leading to a sense of "less content" compared to the refined state CS:GO reached before its retirement. --- Final Verdict Counter-Strike 2 is a foundation-level upgrade. It successfully brings the franchise into the modern era with better visuals and smarter utility mechanics. However, it still carries the weight of a transition period. While the core gameplay remains the "gold standard" of tactical shooters, the community is still waiting for Valve to refine the anti-cheat and bring back the depth of content that made the previous iteration feel so complete. --- As you continue to climb the Premier ranks and manage your current loadout, do you feel that the recent balance patches have significantly impacted your personal playstyle or weapon preferences?

I've got 500-something hours. I play every day usually, it's a huge addiction of mine. If I haven't played for a bit, I start to really miss the game. I love the concept of an eldritch horror keeping people trapped in this cycle of matches trials, and I wish they would make little short videos of the characters interacting at the campfire between matches. I think that would be adorable. Since you play with and against other people, every match is different. Everyone plays a little different and I love the funny moments, the stealth killer jump scares, and I love that I can play with my duo and other friends. It takes real work to get good at this game. It's so rewarding to improve your looping, chasing, etc. skills. I've been playing for over a year and I am finally getting good in chase. But obviously there is always room to improve. I look forward to seeing how my patching changes with experience. A lot of it has to do with learning to think how the other thinks and predicting their decision making split second. I love that. It's so cat and mouse. The cosmetics are great and I love how many characters there are, and the lore. 2v8 is a blast when it's around, I wish they would make it a permanent option, or at the very least let us do custom lobby 2v8 so people can kill bots together. There are some issues, unfortunately. The hit boxes are sometimes really too large or small, and if a killer has bad connection, you might be far ahead of them and it still recognizes it as a hit, not a miss, since on the killer's screen you're within range due to lag. Some maps are horrendous to play, such as midwich or hawkins lab. They should really have done an outdoor map for stranger things. Or perhaps a mall map. Something that isn't so narrow with nowhere to loop. There just aren't enough windows, and once the pallets are gone, there's nothing you can do. And being forced to run down a hallway on either map can be a death sentence if you're against a projectile user. Some of this community is extremely toxic, too. If you're unlucky, you'll get tunneled out and not even play the match. Sometimes survivors are really mean to killers, like they are mad if you 4k or mad if you don't do well in the match, even if you're new to a killer. People are nasty in the comments, so turn them off if you can't handle it. And there's a lot of judgement and stereotypes for playing certain characters that is simply unfounded and uncalled for. I've also encountered people being rude because I am a woman, which is super small minded and silly. It's 2026 people, it shouldn't be a shocker that women, who have the same hands as men do, can play video games. My gender doesn't affect whether I can press buttons in the right order lol. There's quite a bit of 'free' cosmetic content so long as you save up iridescent shards that you earn by simply playing matches. You can also use shards to get some characters. All licenced characters are each about 5 which adds up after a bit, especially on the survivor side if you're trying to get different perks for a build. It sucks to have to pay 5 for a survivor you don't want to play as, because you need one of the three perks they have. It would be great to have an option to buy specific perks on their own, but whatever. I recommend this game if you're a chill person who doesn't get angry with teammates for making mistakes or being purposefully bad sabotaging the match. Or if you like the idea of chasing or being chased and trying to outwit people. Lots of mind games happen in the higher mmr matches. I don't recommend this game to you if you easily get hurt by others or upset by people not doing things the way you wanted. There are going to be bad plays by teammates, whether on accident or on purpose. It's a game. There is no point getting upset over it, especially if it's a genuine mistake that someone made. We've all accidentally dropped a pallet when trying to heal a downed survivor. And sometimes you just have a bad match. If you're the type to tell someone to hurt themselves or uninstall for accidents and mistakes, we do not need you in this community. Be polite, be respectful, and let the game be what it should be: fun! Enjoy your loops, get that cosmetic drip for your main, and may your skill checks be wide and your heals be fast. Have a blast!

The gunplay feels good, movement is smooth, and when you get a fair match, it's genuinely fun. The problem is that fair matches feel harder and harder to find. The amount of cheaters I've encountered is ridiculous. I've seen players blatantly cheating, openly admitting they're using hacks, and still playing without any fear of getting banned. Whether it's wallhacks, aim assistance, or other obvious cheats, it completely ruins the competitive experience. Buying Prime doesn't seem to solve the problem either. On top of that, there are far too many trolls, griefers, and throwers who intentionally ruin matches for everyone else. Nothing kills the enjoyment faster than being stuck in a game with teammates who don't care about winning and are only there to waste everyone's time. What makes it worse is that Valve's anti-cheat system feels ineffective. It often seems like cheaters can play for long periods without consequences, which makes legitimate players wonder why they should even bother taking matches seriously. CS2 has the foundation of a great game, but right now it's being dragged down by cheaters, trolls, and poor enforcement. Until Valve properly addresses these issues, it's difficult to recommend.

h1 Foreword h1 I'm going to preface this quick review by stating that I love Dead by Daylight, and have loved this game since I started playing this game back on console in 2018 (when it became a PS Plus title) and loved it so much that I bought every DLC that didn't already come with the PS4 edition. That being said, there have been an outstanding number of issues that have plagued this game for the entire 10 years of release - some old issues that were fixed while new issues that would arise as the game furthered in development. h1 The Review h1 First and foremost, Dead by Daylight is b NOT b a game that offers a reliable new player experience. The tutorial has seen some changes over the years and only manages to explain the core mechanics of the game in a vacuum. It is a barebones experience. The game itself can be fun once you can wrap your head around the overwhelming amount of perks, perk combinations, maps and map tiles, and the Killers as well as their unique powers. There is so much to this game that it is impossible for someone to learn precisely how to play this game in an efficient and fun manner without needing to rely on guides or feedback from other players (and I will get to the "other players" part.) The game is riddled with bugs, and with every bug that gets squashed - if it doesn't already take multiple years to do so - there's a new one that pops up. Some bugs have never been fixed (looking at you, Twins and Knight) and are usually the result of a game engine that was recently updated but still manages to break more things than it fixed. Balancing for the game, which is quoted by Behavior Interactive "a fun party game you can play with your friends," is completely thrown out the window in favor of... you know I don't even know i what i BHVR's thought process is behind the lack of proper balancing, really. The matchmaking system, or "MMR system" this game has is fundamentally broken, giving you arbitrary, invisible points based off of individual escapes as a Survivor player and 3 kills as a Killer, while taking i away i those points should you be sacrificed to the Entity as a Survivor or you kill less than 3 people as a Killer. Most games after your initial 10-20 games as a fresh account, you b will b be placed against players around your skill level but the more you play the game, the less consistent this will become. I, as someone with over 1,000 hours now on PC alone with a healthy amount of those hours being split between both roles, have been placed against people of vastly different skill levels in every game I play. This also brings me to the b community. b Now, while this does not apply to every single player in the game and there are some amazing members of said community, it cannot be ignored that this game's community is u toxic. u I am talking the same levels of toxicity that have plagued games like League of Legends and Rainbow 6: Siege. It is a community that is riddled with people who have an "Us vs. Them" mentality, who barely understand the core fundamentals of the game (to no real fault of their own,) where they consistently bicker and moan about game mechanics that are used as they're intended to be. As a Survivor player, you'll have Killers who will dominate you and your team, and proceed to "WS" (basically pressing forward then back, repeatedly) on your downed body and refuse to hook you because you blinded them once with a flashlight. Those players are also - usually - extremely toxic in the endgame chat. The community is by far the worst aspect of this game and it's painful for me to even write this because I also love a lot of members of the community who are content creators that try their best to foster a healthier, more nuanced approach to the game. If you're someone who is brand new to Dead by Daylight, reads this review and you still want to buy and play the game then I urge you to proceed with caution and have the understanding that you will not pick up this game and "get it" in just a few hours, nor a few hundred hours. I highly recommend looking up outside sources to learning the game while you're taking the time to play it, as it will help you immensely in beginning to understand the complexity of this game. I recommend playing with friends (if you choose to play Survivor more than Killer) who already have a good amount of experience with the game and if you don't have those, peeking into the Dead by Daylight Discord or finding a community that you can play with because that also helps to enjoy the game more. If you're someone who intends on playing Killer more than Survivor, I cannot stress enough how important it is to be patient and take the time to look up guides on the Killer you want to play the most. Killers are the most unique thing about this game and every single one of them has pros and cons to them. I won't get into the whole tier-list thing that you'll inevitably run into because that's a whole can of worms by itself, but just know that some killers are fundamentally stronger than others by nature of their kits, but that doesn't mean you can't have fun with the weaker ones either. Your experience with the game is going to depend on a lot of factors, so much so that I can't write out all of them in order to properly explain how the game will speak to you. This is all to say that at the end of the day, I cannot in good faith recommend this game to a brand new player who is interested in getting into this game. There are better games out there, with healthier communities that you can be part of if you're looking for that sort of thing. If you're still intending on buying and playing Dead by Daylight, then by all means do so. The game at it's core can be a fun experience and the learning aspect of the game is always what kept me coming back to keep playing. It's an extremely unique game in a market that's oversaturated by the same boring genres, I honestly just wish that BHVR did a better job at both communicating with it's community as well as properly listening to that community when the voices that need to be heard the most are desperately trying to communicate the major issues the game has.
